notes:
WRITE SUCCEEDED ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT. Comment id 1308, text '__mcp-probe-trtc-comment-2026-09-18T07:40:04Z', posted on TR-9062 / TC-54458 (numeric case id 1975349, mapping id 2150387254, project int 379335744). This is permanent residue -- deletes are refused as destructive and cannot be undone through this surface.

Baseline verified myself (not just trusting the sibling's sweep): list_test_run_test_case_comments_v1 on this exact row returned count 0 before the write. After the write, the same read returned count 1 with the identical object (same id 1308, same text, same created_at 2026-09-18T07:40:14.188Z). Storage genuinely changed -- this is NOT a batch-6-style false success.

=== THE KEY QUESTION THIS PROBE ANSWERS: entity_type ===
The returned entity_type is **'TRTC'**, exactly matching the schema's declared example/description ('TRTC for a comment on a test case inside a test run'). This CONFIRMS the theory laid out in the task: 'TRTC' is the correct value for THIS capability (a genuine run-scoped test-case comment), and its presence on the sibling add_test_case_comment_v1's schema (which actually returns entity_type 'TestCase' at runtime) was a copy-paste of this capability's correct value onto the wrong, non-run-scoped capability. Both schemas share verbatim text ('the published spec wraps it under an extra comment key that the server does not send' on the comment field, and the entity_type example/description) -- strong evidence of a shared/duplicated schema fragment where only this capability's copy is accurate.

=== entity_id ===
The returned entity_id is **6809361**. This is NEITHER the mappingId we sent (2150387254) NOR the test_case_id (1975349) NOR the test_run's TR-9062 numeric form -- it is a distinct integer not otherwise observable from this call's own inputs. The schema describes entity_id as 'Id of the run/case mapping cell the comment is attached to -- not the test case id and not the run id.' Taken literally as 'the mapping cell id', one would expect it to equal the mappingId query param (2150387254) we supplied to select that exact cell -- it does not. So either (a) 'mappingId' (the query param, used to route the write to the right configuration cell) and 'entity_id' (the id TM's comment table actually stores against) are two different internal id spaces for the same logical cell -- plausible, since one could be a public/external mapping id and the other an internal foreign key row id -- or (b) the description is simply imprecise about what entity_id numerically equals. Either way, a caller cannot use the description to predict entity_id from mappingId, which is DRIFT (description does not let you verify or derive the field's value), even though the field itself is present and internally consistent (identical entity_id 6809361 on the immediate response and on re-read).

=== Field-by-field check of the stored comment against the declared item shape (id/user_id{id,full_name,email}/group_id/project_id/parent_id/entity_id/entity_type/created_at/comment/edited/is_editable/review_status) ===
- id: present, integer (1308). Matches.
- user_id: present, object with id (2522, int), full_name ('ing'), email ('ing@bsstag.com'). Matches.
- group_id: present, integer (2615). Matches (again ABSENT from the flat top-level 'returns' array despite being in the nested schema and the real response -- reconfirms the standing 'flat returns array is unreliable' pattern, consistent with the case-comment sibling).
- project_id: present, integer (379335744), matches the path param. Matches.
- parent_id: present, null. Matches declared 'always null through this path'.
- entity_id: present, integer (6809361) -- present as declared, but see the dedicated section above: its numeric relationship to mappingId is undocumented/unverifiable. Flagged as drift.
- entity_type: present, 'TRTC', exactly as declared. Matches -- and resolves the cross-capability question (see above).
- created_at: present, ISO datetime ('2026-09-18T07:40:14.188Z'). Matches.
- comment: present, string, returned verbatim as sent (plain text, no HTML added since none was sent). Matches.
- edited: present, boolean, false. Matches.
- is_editable: present, boolean, true. Matches.
- review_status: ABSENT, consistent with the schema's own caveat that it only appears on review-verdict comments -- correctly absent, not counted as declared_missing.
No undeclared fields were returned beyond the declared comment-object properties, and none of the declared properties were missing (review_status is conditional, not required, so its absence is not declared_missing).

=== json_path lesson ===
Again confirms the standing lesson: declared json_path is '/comment/comment' (implying a nested {comment:{comment:...}} body), and the schema itself admits this ('the published spec wraps it under an extra comment key that the server does not send'). The working call sent a FLAT body {comment:'...'} and succeeded on the first attempt; a nested body was not tried since the schema's own admission plus the standing lesson both pointed the same way.

=== Bare-integer test_run_id side experiment ===
Tested once as invited by the task (attempt 2, arguments/result recorded above): sending test_run_id as a deliberately-implausible bare integer (99999999) produced a clean 400 'TRTC not found for given testrun_id:99999999, testcase_id:1975349, mapping_id:2150387254' -- the error message echoes back exactly the bogus id sent. This does NOT reproduce the read sibling's specific defect pattern (where a bare integer resolved to an unrelated real record, id ...358823..., and the error message named that unrelated id instead of the one sent). So for THIS write capability, at least with this one probed integer, the failure mode observed was a straightforward not-found rather than a silent misroute -- though this is a single data point against a single implausible integer, not a disproof of the read-side finding, since a real (rather than implausible) bare integer id was not available to try safely against a write endpoint.

=== Error envelope ===
The attempt-2 400 body was flat {success:false, message:'...'} -- NOT the declared {success:false, error:{code, message, details}} shape. This is consistent with the systemic error-envelope drift already catalogued elsewhere in this suite (nine capabilities, six shapes) rather than a new finding, but is recorded here per instructions to quote verbatim.

=== Verdict rationale ===
DRIFT: (1) entity_id's relationship to the documented 'mapping cell id' (mappingId) is not verifiable/derivable from the description as written -- a caller following the schema literally would expect entity_id == mappingId, and it does not; (2) group_id is present in the real response but absent from the flat 'returns' array (same pattern as the case-comment sibling). Neither is severe: the write itself is fully reliable (no false success, confirmed via independent re-read), and the headline entity_type question is fully and cleanly RESOLVED IN THE SCHEMA'S FAVOR for this capability (entity_type is correctly 'TRTC' here, confirming the copy-paste theory about the sibling capability rather than indicting this one). Severity of both drift items: low-moderate, documentation-accuracy only.
